thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — customer reported vendor advisory for an HSM firmware issue that may affect BYOK signing/attestation (CVE-2026-XXXX). Could impact supply-chain signing flows. We need quick triage: RBAC changes, audit log extraction, KMS fallback options. Who can drive this?
kelly: Is the advisory public or an internal report? link?
sanjay: Vendor sent advisory + CVE and a short repro. Sharing link in DM; customer saw an attestation mismatch after firmware update. Not public yet.
maria: Immediate plan from security side: 1) disable auto firmware updates on affected clusters; 2) enable verbose audit collection for wrap/unwrap/attestation events; 3) rotate any ephemeral wrapping keys; 4) prepare failover to unaffected KMS/HSM pools.
raj: RBAC angle: restrict any role that has both WrapKey and ExportKey privileges. Move to JIT approval for hsm-admin. Also add a temporary deny policy for export across tenants.
sanjay: Do we have a one-liner query to list principals with wrap+export rights across accounts so we can notify owners?
kelly: Yep — can run a config + log query. Example audit query to find wrap calls:
```
resource.type=\"cloud_hsm_key\" protoPayload.methodName=\"WrapKey\"
```
and correlate with principal identifier. I'll run it against prod-eu cluster now.
ops-bot: ALERT: 3 wrap/unwrap attempts from single principal detected within 5s on hsm-prod-eu. Incident created: #6150000012. :rotating_light:
maria: Also collect attestation objects from HSMs ASAP. If attestation chain fails we need to move customer keys to vetted hardware and rotate CMKs. For BYOK customers we must notify legal/compliance and offer a rewrap and full audit package.
sanjay: Drafting customer notification — want it short. Any suggestions?
maria: Suggested copy: "We detected potential integrity issues with a third-party HSM firmware. We're investigating; your keys have not been extracted. As a precaution we can offer a vetted rewrap to unaffected HSMs and provide an audit package. Contact support@redwood.com to opt-in."
raj: Note for vuln triage: if vendor says exploit requires operator-level access, we must call out operator scopes and provide forensic options. Could trigger external attestations.
kelly: Quick oncall checklist for logs: run wrap events export and inspect attestation field. Example:
```
# GCP logging example
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName=\"WrapKey\" AND resource.labels.cluster=\"hsm-prod-eu\"' --limit 100
# check protoPayload.request.integrity.attestation
```
Also capture timestamps and principal IDs to correlate with IAM bindings.
security-bot: Reminder: follow BYOK incident runbook: https://redwood-internal/security/incident-byok. Flag PCI/PHI if any keys protect regulated data and loop Legal immediately.
sanjay: Action assignment: @kelly run principal+wrap query and collect logs; @raj prepare RBAC remediation PR (deny export, JIT for admin); @maria draft customer message and loop Legal/Compliance. I'll engage vendor and update here.
kelly: Query done (results DM'd to Sanjay). Found 2 principals with wrap+export roles in prod-eu. Uploaded logs to secure-share and marked sensitive.
ops-bot: Incident #6150000012 status updated: triage in-progress. Severity P2 until vendor confirms exploitability.
maria: Scheduling a 30m warroom with Legal & Compliance and oncall. Calendar invite sent.
sanjay: One more Q on KMS integration fallback: prefer kms-proxy + soft-wrap to avoid key material leaving customer boundary. Raj — is that compatible with current clients?
raj: Yes, kms-proxy supports soft-wrap profiles and can act as an intermediary for signing without exporting raw key material. Will detail compatibility notes and config in PR.
sanjay: Good. Keep updates here and post any new vendor findings. If this escalates we'll open a formal incident postmortem and update SLA impact. :thumbsup:
